the phosphatidylinositide phosphatidylinostide 3-phosphate (PI(3)) controls cytokinesis through recruitment of the FYVE-CENT complex, and that PI(3) kinase III and the FYVE-CEN complex are involved in the control of cytokinesis.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the molecular mechanisms underlying the formation and function of a key organelle of eukaryotic cells - the midbody - which is formed during the final stage of cell division and is essential for the completion of cytokinesis.
the role of the PI(3)P phosphoinositide in cytokinesis, a process that is essential for the correct segregation of the genetic material into two daughter cells during cell division.
the regulation of cytokinesis by phosphoinositide signalling.

PtdIns3P controls cytokinesis by recruiting FYVE-CENT/TTC19/CHMP4B to the midbody.
